caseno: Civil Petition For Leave to Appeal No. 549 of 2007.
lawyer:
For the Petitioner: Mr. Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record. 
For the Respondents: None Represented.
parties:
Azam Khan Chowdhury Waqf Estate, represented by its Official Mutwalli-Al Haj Shah Shajjadur Rahman ------ Petitioner. 
Versus
The Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and others ------ Respondents.
full_judgment: 5. Mr. Nurul Islam Bhuiyan learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing for the petitioner submitted the petitioner challenged the impugned tender notices Annexures-E, El and G to the writ petition to be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. The High Court Division having not gone into the merit of the case for ascertaining as to whether the impugned tender notices so far it relates to the Annexures-E, El and G to the writ petition were issue4 without any lawful authority most wrongly discharged the Rule on the ground of infructuous occasioning irreparable loss and injury to the petitioner; that the High Court Division having not taken into consideration the facts and circumstances and documentary evidences of the Waqf Estate in question regarding right, title, interest and possession of the Waqf Estate over the disputed hat, bazars and jalmahal vide the Annexures-E, El and G mostly wrongly discharged the Rule on the sole ground of infructuous; that Bhumi Appeal Board, Section 2, in Case No.2-40/2003 Appeal (Sunamganj) in Case No.2-41/2003 Appeal (Sunamganj) and in Case No.2- 42/2003 Appeal (Sunamganj) in three judgments as marked Annexures-D, D I and D2 clearly stated and directed that the disputed property of the appeals are the property of Azam Khan Chowdhury Waqf Estate. The learned Advocate further submitted that the Court below in the judgment dated 30.11.1966 in the suit No.30 of 1964 declared that the issue of Certificate for realization of rent from tenants of the plaintiff Waqf Estate is illegal and without jurisdiction for the time being and until Estate Vs. Gust of Bangladesh & Ors 19BLT (AD) 2011 further orders from the Government defendant are also hereby restrained from interfering with the plaintiff possession of the Shariat Mohal and Khas Mohal of the Waqf Estate from the date of this judgment, the Government did nothing as to the said property till today through which-it is clearly evident that the properties in question vide the Annexure-E, Eland G are the property of the said Waqf Estate. Accordingly, discharging the Rule in the Writ Petition No.1324 of 2004 only on infructuous grounds has caused serious prejudice to the petitioner.
